The correct answer is 171, so Solution 2 is the one with the right final answer.

**Criterion.** A response $v$ is consistent with a prime $p$ iff $v$ is well defined on residues mod $p$ and either some residue mod $p$ is unqueried or $v$ is nonconstant. Ana wins for a pair $(p,q)$ iff the join of the mod-$p$ and mod-$q$ partitions of the queried points is a single block and at least one of $p,q$ has all its residues queried.

**Lower bound.** At most one prime can fail to have all residues covered, since two such primes admit a constant response consistent with both. If all primes below 100 except $p_0$ are fully covered, then each fully covered pair $(p,q)$ needs a connected bipartite graph on $p+q$ residue vertices, so $n \ge p+q-1$. The worst case is $p_0 = 97$, which leaves the pair $(83,89)$ with $n \ge 171$. Other choices of $p_0$ give 179 or 185, so $n \ge 171$.

**Upper bound.** Take $x_i = 97i$ for $i = 0,\dots,170$. Then every $x_i \equiv 0 \pmod{97}$, so 97 is never fully covered and its partition is trivial, which makes every pair involving 97 connected. For primes $p,q \le 89$, the residues of $97i$ mod $p$ and mod $q$ give the same partitions as $i \bmod p$ and $i \bmod q$. By the Fine–Wilf theorem, the graph on $\{0,\dots,L-1\}$ with edges $i \sim i+p$ and $i \sim i+q$ is connected once $L \ge p+q-1$. The largest such requirement is $83+89-1 = 171$, so all pairs are connected.

Solution 1 (186) and Solution 3 (185) both overcount, since they assume all primes must be fully covered. My recollection of 181 as the answer does not match this derivation, so I am relying on the argument above.

CHOICE: 2
